chapter.title: Time
chapter.para: JetOS keeps the time of the module and gives it to the scheduler and to the partitions.

section.title: SRQ-JET-TIME-001
section.para: JetOS shall maintain a system time, in nanoseconds since the start of the module, that never decreases.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: The time windows of the partitions, the time-outs and the periods of the processes are all measured against one clock.

section.title: SRQ-JET-TIME-002
section.para: JetOS shall give the system time to a partition that asks for the time of the real-time clock, and shall refuse a request for any other clock with an error.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: The partition library builds its time services on the system time; no other clock exists in the module.

section.title: SRQ-JET-TIME-003
section.para: JetOS shall give the calendar time, in seconds, to a partition that asks for it: the calendar time read at the start of the module plus the system time.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: Partitions need the date for logs and time stamps, and it has to advance with the system time.

section.title: SRQ-JET-TIME-004
section.para: JetOS shall re-evaluate its scheduling decisions at every tick of a periodic timer of the board, whose frequency is fixed when JetOS is built.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: The ends of the time windows and the time-outs take effect within one tick period of their time.
